raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Adds `dspark_fused_topk_walk` (off by default): with `dspark_draft_topk`, DSpark's sequential Markov walk over the top-k candidates runs in one Triton launch per request instead of ~100 small kernels, and the two full-vocabulary passes per decode step (`fill_(-inf)` and the per-step `gumbel_sample`) are removed. Builds on the top-k projection from #49969.

## Claims

Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 + DSpark drafter (8 draft tokens, top-k 64, probabilistic), 1x H100:

- `vllm bench serve` (Spec-Bench, temperature 0.6, 6 interleaved fresh-server pairs): **TPOT −1.3% (mean) and −2.3% (p99) at concurrency 32, output throughput +1.5%**, better in 6/6 pairs; TPOT −1.4% (mean) at concurrency 1.
- `vllm bench forward`: decode step **150–370 µs faster (0.72–0.95%)** for batch 1–32.
- The Markov top-k sampling path itself (everything after the draft lm_head): **242 → 92 µs at batch 1, 1121 → 578 µs at batch 32**; ncu: 105 → 17 kernels, DRAM traffic 700 → 419 MB at batch 32. What remains is mostly `torch.topk` (untouched).
- Lossless: the kernel samples exactly the bf16 values it writes to the draft logits cache. Draft logits differ from the per-step loop by at most 1 bf16 ULP (accumulation order of the 256-wide dot); GSM8K accuracy and acceptance length unchanged.

## Validation

**Serving** (`vllm serve Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 --max-num-seqs 32 --max-model-len 8192 --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark",...,"num_speculative_tokens":8,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","dspark_draft_topk":64}'`, then `vllm bench serve --dataset-name spec_bench --temperature 0.6 --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,95,99`, 200 prompts at concurrency 1, 1000 at concurrency 32). Each run starts a fresh server; GPU 1 ran loop/fused × 3, GPU 2 fused/loop × 3. Δ is the mean over the 6 adjacent pairs with a 95% t-interval; "6/6" = fused better in every pair:

| | c=1 loop | c=1 fused | Δ | c=32 loop | c=32 fused | Δ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TPOT mean (ms) | 4.33 | 4.27 | −1.41 ±0.94% (6/6) | 11.50 | 11.36 | −1.28 ±0.94% (6/6) |
| TPOT p50 | 4.28 | 4.26 | −0.62 ±1.89% | 11.43 | 11.27 | −1.39 ±1.13% (6/6) |
| TPOT p90 | 5.77 | 5.55 | −3.89 ±2.47% (6/6) | 15.45 | 15.24 | −1.32 ±1.34% |
| TPOT p95 | 6.14 | 5.93 | −3.49 ±3.38% | 16.81 | 16.50 | −1.84 ±1.95% |
| TPOT p99 | 6.88 | 6.61 | −3.90 ±4.18% | 19.30 | 18.86 | −2.27 ±1.95% (6/6) |
| ITL p50 (ms) | 17.51 | 17.35 | −0.89 ±0.27% (6/6) | 38.25 | 37.88 | −0.97 ±0.34% (6/6) |
| output tok/s | 204.7 | 208.2 | +1.71 ±2.10% | 1843 | 1870 | +1.51 ±0.69% (6/6) |
| acceptance length | 3.98 | 4.01 | +0.73 ±0.64% | 4.04 | 4.04 | +0.07 ±0.40% |

A first serving run with only two long-lived servers per GPU was dominated by a ~2–5% drift between the first and second half of the session, which is why the comparison above alternates fresh servers.

**Decode step** (`vllm bench forward --model Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 --max-num-seqs 32 --max-model-len 8192 --speculative-config '{...same...}' --case bN=N*9@4096:8`, median µs; two H100s, arms interleaved A D D A / D A A D, 2 runs each):

| batch | loop (GPU 1) | fused (GPU 1) | Δ GPU 1 | Δ GPU 2 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 20481 | 20329 | −152 (0.74%) | −152 (0.74%) |
| 2 | 21693 | 21511 | −182 (0.84%) | −178 (0.82%) |
| 4 | 23062 | 22879 | −184 (0.80%) | −207 (0.90%) |
| 8 | 26483 | 26231 | −252 (0.95%) | −246 (0.93%) |
| 16 | 34365 | 34041 | −324 (0.94%) | −324 (0.94%) |
| 32 | 51165 | 50792 | −373 (0.73%) | −367 (0.72%) |

<details>
<summary>Sampling path alone: CUDA events and ncu</summary>

Everything after the draft lm_head (`topk`, cache fill, 8 Markov steps) captured as one CUDA graph, real W1/W2 (V = 248,320, rank 256), 256 MB L2 flush before each replay; CUDA events (200 replays, median) and ncu node mode (kernel replay, per replay):

| batch | loop µs | fused µs | kernels | Σ kernel time µs (ncu) | DRAM R+W MB (ncu) | walk kernel µs (ncu) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 242 | 92 | 81 → 17 | 331 → 111 | 18 → 13 | 24.4 |
| 2 | 311 | 105 | 105 → 17 | 455 → 128 | 35 → 25 | 24.9 |
| 4 | 378 | 139 | 105 → 17 | 538 → 166 | 70 → 49 | 25.2 |
| 8 | 514 | 196 | 105 → 17 | 662 → 223 | 166 → 107 | 25.3 |
| 16 | 799 | 339 | 105 → 17 | 933 → 352 | 334 → 210 | 25.4 |
| 32 | 1121 | 578 | 105 → 17 | 1270 → 597 | 700 → 419 | 25.8 |

14 of the 17 remaining kernels and 80–564 µs are `torch.topk`. The 89 replaced kernels per step at batch 32 (ncu): `fill_` 40 µs / 123 MB written, W1/W2 gathers 77 µs, `clone` 28 µs, `baddbmm` 33 µs, `scatter_`/`gather` 106 µs, small index/copy kernels 69 µs, `_gumbel_sample_kernel` 292 µs / 154 MB, block argmax 52 µs.

Walk kernel tuning (CUDA events, L2 flushed, top-k 64): chunked rank loop with 4 warps 47–49 µs; 2 warps 40–41 µs; prefetching the next step's W2 tile with the full rank and 8 warps 27–28 µs (used).
</details>

**Correctness**

- `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark_topk.py`: fused walk vs the per-step loop with Markov weights chosen so every product and sum is exact in fp32, so tokens and the whole draft-logits cache must match **bit for bit**: temperature 0 / 0.7 / 1.0, fp32 and fp64 Gumbel, a CUDA-graph padding row (`idx_mapping = -1`), permuted request slots, top-k 12 (masked block), and a batch-sharded cache (2 shards, rank 1). A replay test checks no stale candidate survives after half of each slot's candidates change, and a greedy test (no draft-logits cache) also checks the confidence-head inputs. Disabling the stale-candidate clear or the shard row mapping makes them fail. 25 passed.
- Real Qwen3.8 W1/W2, 8 seeds × batch 1/8/32 × temperature 0/0.6/1.0: cache entries differ by ≤ 1 bf16 ULP on 1.5–1.9% of candidates; a token differs only at a step whose logits differ; 251–256 of 256 rows identical over all 8 steps.
- Regression: `test_dspark_topk.py`, `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_gumbel_sample.py`, `test_dflash2.py`, `test_lilicorr.py`, `tests/watermarking/test_gumbel.py`, `test_rejection_sampler_utils.py`, `tests/transformers_utils/test_speculators_dspark_config.py`: 303 passed.

**GSM8K** (`pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dspark/test_dspark.py`, Qwen3-4B-FP8 + `deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_4b_block7`, 1319 questions, temperature 1.0, top-k 64, H100):

| | accuracy | acceptance rate | acceptance length |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| per-step loop | 0.796 | 0.422 | 3.951 |
| `dspark_fused_topk_walk` (new e2e case) | 0.792 | 0.425 | 3.976 |
| `dspark_fused_topk_walk`, rebased on `f8f7634cb4` | 0.796 | 0.428 | 3.998 |
| existing full-vocab references (12 runs) | 0.782–0.814 | 0.418–0.434 | 3.928–4.037 |

## Details

- **Kernel** (`dspark/topk_walk.py`): grid = (num_reqs,), 8 warps. Each program walks the draft steps: `W1[prev]` → dot with the `W2[ids]` tile (64 × rank, prefetched during the previous step since the candidate ids are known up front, so only the `W1[prev]` load is on the serial chain) → fp32 accumulate → one bf16 rounding of `values + scale * bias` (as `baddbmm` does) → write the 64 values to the cache → Gumbel-max over the 64 candidates with the same noise helpers, seed (`spec_step_seed`), position and token-id keys as `gumbel_sample`; ties go to the smallest token id like the dense argmax, and a NaN score falls back to the argmax's own candidate so `prev` always stays a valid id. `gumbel_noised_argmax` is split into `gumbel_noised_logits` + max so the kernel can tie-break by id; behaviour of existing callers is unchanged.
- **Sparse cache maintenance**: when the walk is in use, `draft_logits` is filled with `-inf` once (`draft_logits_spec`), and the walk keeps the k ids it wrote per (slot, step) and resets exactly those before writing new ones, the same scheme as DFlash2's `_cache_draft_logits_kernel` but inside the walk so it costs no extra launch. A `tl.debug_barrier()` separates the reset from the writes because an id can be both stale and new. Only the DSpark sampler writes `draft_logits`, so the invariant holds.
- **Batch-sharded draft logits (#63554)** are supported: like `gumbel_sample` and DFlash2, the walk writes (and resets) only the rows this rank owns, at `shard_row(req_state)`.
- **Confidence head** still works: its Markov embeddings are computed once from `[anchor, draft_tokens[:, :-1]]` for both the fused and the per-step path.
- **Falls back** to the per-step loop (one warning at load) for a reduced draft vocabulary (d2t, greedy or probabilistic), draft watermarking, the online acceptance estimator, a quantized/retained-NVFP4 `markov_w2`, or a `top_k × rank` tile above 128 × 256 (larger tiles spill registers). Weights are read from the Markov modules at launch, so weight reloads are picked up.
- No CPU–GPU sync added: no host reads, fixed buffers, safe under FULL CUDA graphs (validated by the replay test and the e2e and serving runs).
- **Not a duplicate**: #62958 (int8 W2 walk) and #63181 (ROCm fused GEMV + epilogue) cover the full-vocabulary path and do not apply with `dspark_draft_topk`; #61869 is the DSv4.1 specialized decode. #56694 also edits `_sample_sequential_topk`, but changes the candidate set (base ∪ Markov top-k) rather than fusing the walk; the two would conflict textually and the kernel would need the union candidates if #56694 lands. Happy to coordinate with its author.
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write the kernel, tests and measurements.

---

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""DSpark top-k Markov walk in one launch.
+
+Equivalent to the ``_sample_sequential_topk`` loop for an unquantized Markov
+head: per request, correct the top-k base logits with ``W2[ids] @ W1[prev]``,
+cache the corrected candidates and sample one of them, for every draft step.
+The draft logits cache keeps ``-inf`` outside the candidates by clearing the
+ids written by the previous walk on the same request slot, so no full-vocab
+pass remains after the top-k.
+"""
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.batch_shard import shard_owner, shard_row
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.gumbel import gumbel_noised_logits, spec_step_seed
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _topk_markov_walk_kernel(
+    base_values_ptr,
+    candidate_ids_ptr,
+    anchor_ids_ptr,
+    markov_w1_ptr,
+    markov_w1_stride,
+    markov_w2_ptr,
+    markov_w2_stride,
+    idx_mapping_ptr,
+    sample_pos_ptr,
+    temperature_ptr,
+    seeds_ptr,
+    draft_tokens_ptr,
+    draft_tokens_stride,
+    draft_logits_ptr,
+    draft_logits_stride_0,
+    draft_logits_stride_1,
+    cached_ids_ptr,
+    scale,
+    RANK: tl.constexpr,
+    NUM_STEPS: tl.constexpr,
+    TOP_K: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_K: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_R: tl.constexpr,
+    SAMPLE_PROBABILISTIC: tl.constexpr,
+    USE_FP64: tl.constexpr,
+    CACHE_NUM_SHARDS: tl.constexpr,
+    CACHE_SHARD_IDX: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    row = tl.program_id(0)
+    k = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_K)
+    k_mask = k < TOP_K
+    r = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_R)
+    req_state = tl.load(idx_mapping_ptr + row * NUM_STEPS).to(tl.int64)
+    valid = req_state >= 0
+    # A batch-sharded cache holds only this rank's requests, packed by row.
+    cache_mask = (
+        k_mask & valid & (shard_owner(req_state, CACHE_NUM_SHARDS) == CACHE_SHARD_IDX)
+    )
+    cache_row = shard_row(req_state, CACHE_NUM_SHARDS) * draft_logits_stride_0
+    if SAMPLE_PROBABILISTIC:
+        temperature = tl.load(temperature_ptr + req_state, mask=valid, other=0.0)
+        seed = tl.load(seeds_ptr + req_state, mask=valid, other=0)
+        for step in range(NUM_STEPS):
+            cached = cached_ids_ptr + (req_state * NUM_STEPS + step) * TOP_K + k
+            stale_ids = tl.load(cached, mask=cache_mask, other=0)
+            tl.store(
+                draft_logits_ptr + cache_row + step * draft_logits_stride_1 + stale_ids,
+                float("-inf"),
+                mask=cache_mask,
+            )
+        # A candidate id can be both stale and new; clear before writing.
+        tl.debug_barrier()
+    else:
+        temperature = 0.0
+        seed = 0
+
+    prev = tl.load(anchor_ids_ptr + row).to(tl.int64)
+    r_mask = r < RANK
+    # W2[ids] does not depend on the walk, so each step prefetches the next
+    # step's tile; only the W1[prev] load stays on the serial chain.
+    next_ids = tl.load(
+        candidate_ids_ptr + row * NUM_STEPS * TOP_K + k, mask=k_mask, other=0
+    )
+    next_w = tl.load(
+        markov_w2_ptr + next_ids.to(tl.int64)[:, None] * markov_w2_stride + r[None, :],
+        mask=k_mask[:, None] & r_mask[None, :],
+        other=0.0,
+    )
+    for step in range(NUM_STEPS):
+        flat = row * NUM_STEPS + step
+        ids = next_ids
+        weight = next_w
+        values = tl.load(base_values_ptr + flat * TOP_K + k, mask=k_mask, other=0.0)
+        has_next = step + 1 < NUM_STEPS
+        next_ids = tl.load(
+            candidate_ids_ptr + (flat + 1) * TOP_K + k, mask=k_mask & has_next, other=0
+        )
+        next_w = tl.load(
+            markov_w2_ptr
+            + next_ids.to(tl.int64)[:, None] * markov_w2_stride
+            + r[None, :],
+            mask=(k_mask & has_next)[:, None] & r_mask[None, :],
+            other=0.0,
+        )
+        embed = tl.load(markov_w1_ptr + prev * markov_w1_stride + r, mask=r_mask)
+        bias = tl.sum(weight.to(tl.float32) * embed.to(tl.float32)[None, :], axis=1)
+        # Round once to the cache dtype, as baddbmm does, and sample exactly the
+        # value the rejection sampler will read back.
+        logits = (values.to(tl.float32) + scale * bias).to(values.dtype)
+
+        if SAMPLE_PROBABILISTIC:
+            tl.store(
+                draft_logits_ptr + cache_row + step * draft_logits_stride_1 + ids,
+                logits,
+                mask=cache_mask,
+            )
+            tl.store(
+                cached_ids_ptr + (req_state * NUM_STEPS + step) * TOP_K + k,
+                ids,
+                mask=cache_mask,
+            )
+
+        # sample_pos is the predicted token's position P. Sampling keys a draw
+        # by the position before the sampled token, P-1.
+        pos = tl.load(sample_pos_ptr + flat) - 1
+        scores = gumbel_noised_logits(
+            logits.to(tl.float32),
+            ids,
+            k_mask,
+            spec_step_seed(seed, step),
+            pos,
+            temperature,
+            IS_DRAFTING=True,
+            USE_FP64=USE_FP64,
+        )
+        scores = tl.where(k_mask, scores, float("-inf"))
+        best, best_k = tl.max(scores, axis=0, return_indices=True)
+        # Ties go to the smallest token id, as in the dense argmax. A NaN score
+        # matches nothing; then keep the max's own candidate so prev stays in
+        # range.
+        is_best = k_mask & (scores == best)
+        tied_min = tl.min(tl.where(is_best, ids, 1 << 62), axis=0)
+        best_id = tl.sum(tl.where(k == best_k, ids, 0), axis=0)
+        any_best = tl.sum(is_best.to(tl.int32), axis=0) > 0
+        prev = tl.where(any_best, tied_min, best_id).to(tl.int64)
+        tl.store(draft_tokens_ptr + row * draft_tokens_stride + step, prev)
+
+
+class TopkMarkovWalk:
+    """Runs the DSpark top-k Markov walk and keeps the cached candidate ids."""
+
+    # One program holds two [top_k, rank] W2 tiles; larger ones spill.
+    MAX_TILE = 128 * 256
+
+    @classmethod
+    def supports(cls, top_k: int, rank: int) -> bool:
+        return (
+            triton.next_power_of_2(top_k) * triton.next_power_of_2(rank) <= cls.MAX_TILE
+        )
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        markov_w1: torch.nn.Module,
+        markov_w2: torch.nn.Module,
+        scale: float,
+        max_num_reqs: int,
+        num_steps: int,
+        top_k: int,
+        device: torch.device,
+    ):
+        # Modules, not tensors: weight reloads may rebind their parameters.
+        self.markov_w1 = markov_w1
+        self.markov_w2 = markov_w2
+        self.scale = scale
+        self.num_steps = num_steps
+        self.top_k = top_k
+        # Points at column 0 of every row until the first walk on a slot, which
+        # matches the cache's -inf fill.
+        self.cached_ids = torch.zeros(
+            max_num_reqs, num_steps, top_k, dtype=torch.int64, device=device
+        )
+
+    def sample(
+        self,
+        base_values: torch.Tensor,  # [num_reqs, num_steps, top_k]
+        candidate_ids: torch.Tensor,  # [num_reqs, num_steps, top_k]
+        anchor_ids: torch.Tensor,  # [num_reqs]
+        idx_mapping: torch.Tensor,  # [num_reqs * num_steps]
+        sample_pos: torch.Tensor,  # [num_reqs * num_steps]
+        temperature: torch.Tensor,
+        seeds: torch.Tensor,
+        draft_tokens: torch.Tensor,  # [>= num_reqs, num_steps]
+        draft_logits: torch.Tensor | None,
+        use_fp64: bool,
+        draft_logits_num_shards: int = 1,
+        draft_logits_shard_idx: int = 0,
+    ) -> None:
+        num_reqs = base_values.shape[0]
+        markov_w1 = self.markov_w1.weight
+        markov_w2 = self.markov_w2.weight
+        rank = markov_w1.shape[1]
+        _topk_markov_walk_kernel[(num_reqs,)](
+            base_values.contiguous(),
+            candidate_ids.contiguous(),
+            anchor_ids.contiguous(),
+            markov_w1,
+            markov_w1.stride(0),
+            markov_w2,
+            markov_w2.stride(0),
+            idx_mapping.contiguous(),
+            sample_pos.contiguous(),
+            temperature,
+            seeds,
+            draft_tokens,
+            draft_tokens.stride(0),
+            draft_logits,
+            draft_logits.stride(0) if draft_logits is not None else 0,
+            draft_logits.stride(1) if draft_logits is not None else 0,
+            self.cached_ids,
+            self.scale,
+            RANK=rank,
+            NUM_STEPS=self.num_steps,
+            TOP_K=self.top_k,
+            BLOCK_K=triton.next_power_of_2(self.top_k),
+            BLOCK_R=triton.next_power_of_2(rank),
+            SAMPLE_PROBABILISTIC=draft_logits is not None,
+            USE_FP64=use_fp64,
+            CACHE_NUM_SHARDS=draft_logits_num_shards,
+            CACHE_SHARD_IDX=draft_logits_shard_idx,
+            num_warps=8,
+        )
